title: The constructed reals are a field, and the inverse must be existential because a functional one is undefinable
statement: CReal.fieldS : AlgS.Field makes the constructed reals an instance of the constructive field record, over the existing CReal.commRingS and the existing Bishop apartness CReal.Apart. The load-bearing declaration is CReal.mulInvEx: for every real x apart from zero there EXISTS a real y with x*y equivalent to one. This shape is forced. CReal.inv : (x : CReal) -> (k : Nat) -> PosBound x k -> CReal takes its modulus as DATA; CReal.Apart x zero is Or (lt x zero) (lt zero x), a Prop; and CReal.pos_bound_of_lt yields the modulus only inside an Exists, also a Prop. So neither the sign nor the modulus can be eliminated out into a CReal, and a field field of type (x : carrier) -> apart x zero -> carrier is UNDEFINABLE here -- a large-elimination wall, not a missing lemma (CReal.no_total_inverse already proves the total form impossible). The existential form is a Prop, so both eliminations are legal: the proof is one Or.elim on the sign and one Exists.rec on the modulus per branch. The positive branch is free (pos_bound_of_lt then mul_inv_cancel). The negative branch costs two new theorems: CReal.pos_of_neg_lt_zero (x < 0 gives 0 < -x, one add_lt_add_of_le_of_lt read back through lt_congr) and the sign pushed through the product by AlgS.mul_neg_right, because CReal has only neg_mul_neg, which is squares.

formal.statement: theorem CReal.mulInvEx : ((x0 : CReal) -> ((x1 : CReal.Apart x0 CReal.zero) -> Exists.{1} CReal (fun (x2 : CReal) => CReal.Equiv (CReal.mul x0 x2) CReal.one)))

evidence.supports: CReal.apart_compat, one_apart_zero, pos_of_neg_lt_zero, mulInvEx and fieldS admit with empty footprints, and all five were admitted on FIRST submission. The suite checks that CReal.fieldS's rendered type is exactly AlgS.Field; that mulInvEx's hypothesis really names CReal.Apart (not a disequality) and its conclusion really names Exists; that the AlgS.Field selectors carrier/equiv/zero/one/mul/neg/apart/apartSymm/apartCotrans/mulInvEx at CReal.fieldS reduce by def_eq to CReal's OWN constants -- an evaluation test a wrongly ordered constructor application would fail while still having type AlgS.Field -- and that apart is NOT def_eq to CReal.Equiv. It also infers AlgS.Field.mul_left_cancel at CReal.fieldS, so the generic field theorem demonstrably reaches the reals. One negative control must be REFUSED: pos_of_neg_lt_zero applied with the hypothesis 0 < x rather than x < 0.
evidence.checker_command: out=$(cargo test -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib --release -- creal::field_setoid_instance --test-threads=4 2>&1) && test "$(printf "%s\n" "$out" | grep -cE 'test result: ok\. 7 passed; 0 failed')" -ge 1
evidence.notes: The pinned count is 7 (six behavioural tests plus the ADR-1627 declaration inventory). AlgS.Field.IsTight CReal.fieldS is deliberately ABSENT -- see the notes.

notes: AlgS.Field.IsTight CReal.fieldS is NOT declared. creal.rs's doc block on not_apart_one_of_pow_succ_eq_one calls tightness 'Markov's principle' and that is WRONG -- Markov is the converse, Not (Equiv x y) -> Apart x y, and the apart doc block on the same struct states the direction correctly. Tightness of the Bishop apartness is constructively true; what its proof needs is a single-index introduction rule for CReal.lt (from x_n - y_n > 2/(n+1) produce lt y x with the explicit rational gap), and no such lemma exists among CReal's order theorems. That is why AlgS.Field carries tightness as a predicate rather than as a field: making it a field would have made the reals not a field.
